To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AGE-2 is a novel AGEs that has a causal role in the pathogeneses of diabetic complications and Alzheimer's disease.
AGE-2 is the main structure of TAGES, and that the formation of AGE- 2 is accelerated in vivo in the diabetic patients.
AGE-2, which is a main structure of TAGES (toxic AGE structures), in the serum and brain of diabetic patients has diverse biological activities on the cells of the vascular wall and the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the chemical structure of AGEs, and the elucidation of the mechanisms by which AGE-2 is formed in vivo, and how it contributes to the development of diabetic complications and neurodegenerative disorders.
the identification and characterization of the novel AGE-2, which has been shown to play a critical role in the pathophysiology of diabetic complications and neurodegenerative disorders.
the elucidation of the mechanism(s) for the formation of TAGE-2 and the role of TAGE- 2 in the pathophysiology of diabetic complications and in AD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AGE-2 is a novel marker of the severity of AD and is a potential target for the treatment of AD.
AGE-2 is a novel and specific marker for the diagnosis and monitoring of the progression of AD and diabetic complications.
the formation of AGE-1 and AGE-2 is a complex process involving multiple pathways, which is dependent on the concentration of glyceraldehyde and the type of proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of AGE- 2 is accelerated by increased fluxes of glucose through the glycolytic, polyol and fructose pathways, and by increased levels of glyceraldehyde in the cytosolic and extracellular compartments.
the formation of TAGE (AGE-2) is a major contributor to the pathogenesis of AD and diabetes complications in vivo.
AGE-2 may be a key factor in the pathogenesis and progression of diabetic complications and Alzheimer's disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glyceraldehyde is the key precursor of AGE-2 and that the formation of AGE-1, AGE-2, and AGE-3 is the most important pathway for the formation of TAGE in vivo.
the formation of AGEs is not only the result of the glycation of proteins but also a result of the glycosylation of proteins.

AGE-2, the major TAGE, is formed from glyceraldehyde in vivo, and is present within the AGEs- modified proteins that circulate in diabetic serum, as well as within the AGEs modified proteins that are found in AD brains.
